statement: US export controls keep ByteDance off NVIDIA's advanced chips, so its build-out reportedly leans on Arm and RISC-V custom silicon, Qualcomm inference parts and domestic Chinese suppliers including talks with Iluvatar CoreX and Baidu.
why: One of the largest AI spenders outside the US hyperscalers is routing a very large budget away from merchant GPUs, which caps how much of that spending the leading vendor can capture.

impact.mechanism: Export restrictions divert a major buyer's accelerator budget to custom and domestic silicon, subtracting from merchant-GPU demand while adding to alternative-silicon volume.

evidence.excerpt: Because US export controls limit ByteDance's access to Nvidia's advanced chips, its build-out reportedly runs through custom silicon on Arm and RISC-V, Qualcomm inference parts, and domestic Chinese suppliers

confidence.basis: Single secondary outlet, and the supplier talks are described as under discussion rather than contracted.
